frontier.hypothesis: Loop 2's preheader copy is reachable if loop 2's GUARD BLOCK stops being a join - i.e. if the loop-1 guard's skip path reaches loop 2's guard through its own copy of that guard rather than by branching to a shared label - because then cse's extended basic block would include the load of ctx+0xC and would fold loop 2's redundant re-read into a copy exactly as it does in loop 1.
frontier.mechanism: cse_end_of_basic_block terminates the extended basic block at a label with more than one reference, so the load of `p` that precedes the join is outside cse's window when it processes loop 2's preheader - which is precisely why loop 2's redundant read stays a real `lw` (E-s26-2) while loop 1's folds to a copy. Removing the join removes that boundary.
frontier.next_probe: s12 measured duplicating the WHOLE of loop 2 into both arms of the loop-1 guard at 35 (jump2 does not re-merge). Duplicating only loop 2's GUARD (a 4-instruction test) into the loop-1 skip path, leaving one shared loop body, has never been measured - build it on chassis A and on the candidate chassis and score both. If it is also >= 10, the join is structurally unremovable from C and that closes the last cse-boundary lever.

frontier.hypothesis: Chassis A's two missing copies have a single shared cause that an instrumented-cc1 dump can name, and the dump would either confirm the EBB-boundary explanation for loop 2 or expose a different reason that the C can still address.
frontier.mechanism: On chassis A the residual is exactly 'the two copies and nothing else', which makes it the cleanest chassis yet for a pass-attribution run: loop 1's redundant read is visibly folded-then-deleted (127 -> 126) and loop 2's visibly not folded at all, so .cse and .combine dumps of the SAME build show both fates side by side in one function.
frontier.next_probe: Run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80017848` with body_A.c applied (the instrumented cc1 is tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, NOT build/cc1; re-prove codegen identity with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s15/idump.sh first) and read .cse for whether loop 2's `lw` is even entered in the same qty as `p`, then .combine for loop 1's copy deletion. Cheap, and it either confirms or replaces the EBB-boundary account that this session inferred from behaviour alone.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual's remaining 3 points are the same two points at two sites, so any lever that buys ONE preheader copy for free buys both - and the only known producer (an orphaned cse-folded redundant read, per s9/s15/s16) requires a second use whose price is now measured at every site in the function.
frontier.mechanism: Loop 1 buys its copy for exactly 1 point (the `p = q` tail materialises as `addu a0,a3,zero` where target has `lw a0,12(s2)`); loop 2 cannot buy it at all (19-22 post-loop, 6 in-body, 12 pre-join carrier). The asymmetry is entirely about where a free second use exists, not about the copy mechanism, which is understood.
frontier.next_probe: Any future proposal must name a second-use SITE, not a mechanism - the mechanism is settled. Before spending a cell, price the site against the banked table (post-loop 19-22, in-body 6, pre-join 12, guard-consuming 6-28) and reject anything that adds a live value across loop 2, since target already occupies s0-s5 and a seventh callee-save grows the prologue.
